You can file a Level 1 appeal by contacting the Quality Improvement Organization using the contact information on the Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage or in Chapter 2 of the Evidence of Coverage. [1]
You must make your Level 1 appeal request by noon of the day before the effective date on the Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage. [1]
For a Level 1 appeal, you can request a fast appeal if your health requires it, and the Quality Improvement Organization must give you an answer within 72 hours. [2]
For a standard Level 1 appeal, you must submit your request within 65 calendar days from the date on the written notice of the coverage decision. [2]
If your Level 1 appeal is denied, you can file a Level 2 appeal with the Independent Review Entity within 65 calendar days from the date on the written notice. [3]

A complaint is also called a grievance. [1]
Making a complaint is called filing a grievance. [1]

You can file a grievance in writing if you prefer not to call or are unsatisfied after calling. [1]
If a representative files a grievance on your behalf, they need to provide legally appointed representation or complete an Appointment of Representative form. [1]

You can see out-of-network providers, but your share of the costs may be higher. [1]
Out-of-network providers must be eligible to participate in Medicare for the plan to cover their services. [1]
You don’t need a referral or prior authorization for out-of-network care, but a pre-visit coverage decision is recommended. [1]
If the plan determines that out-of-network services are not covered or medically necessary, you may have to pay the full cost. [1]
For emergency care, urgently needed services, or out-of-area dialysis, you may not have to pay higher cost-sharing for out-of-network providers. [1]
